<awtsmoosMeluketTranslation heichel="ikar" alias="meluket_translation_en" seriesId="כסלו_meluket" postId="BH_POST_1766518915545_theRebbe_780" batchId="meluket-_D7_9B_D7_A1_D7_9C_D7_95_meluket__BH_POST_1766518915545_theRebbe_780__p001">
  <section v="0">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section provides the header and date for the maamar delivered on Tuesday, 15 Kislev 5741 before Minchah.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">B'Siyata Dishmaya.</t>
    <t s="1">Tuesday,</t>
    <t s="2">15 Kislev 5741 – before the afternoon prayer*</t>
  </section>
  <section v="1">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section introduces the verse "He redeemed my soul in peace from battle" and notes the precise interpretations of the Alter Rebbe and the Mitteler Rebbe regarding the emphasis on peace and the phrase "from battle."</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">"He redeemed my soul in peace from battle, for many were with me."</t>
    <t s="1">And known are the precise interpretations of the Alter Rebbe, author of the redemption of 19 Kislev,</t>
    <t s="2">and his son who filled his place, the Mitteler Rebbe, author of the redemption of 10 Kislev,</t>
    <t s="3">in that this verse emphasizes not only the matter of redemption and liberation in general,</t>
    <t s="4">but that the redemption is specifically in peace.</t>
    <t s="5">And also what is said "from battle,"</t>
    <t s="6">and not from war and the like.</t>
    <t s="7">And furthermore, there is precision in saying "from battle" specifically,</t>
    <t s="8">that the redemption is for me.</t>
    <t s="9">Also, one must understand the saying "for many were with me,"</t>
    <t s="10">which implies that this is the reason for "He redeemed my soul in peace" – what is the matter in this?</t>
  </section>
  <section v="2">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section explains that redemption applies only when there is an opposing force, and through redemption from darkness and folly, a qualitative and quantitative advantage of light and wisdom is achieved.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">2)</t>
    <t s="1">And the point of the explanation in this,</t>
    <t s="2">is that redemption applies only when there is an existence of an opposing matter,</t>
    <t s="3">for when there is no existence of an opposing side, there is no need or place for redemption,</t>
    <t s="4">since holiness is the only path and the only reality,</t>
    <t s="5">but when there is an opposing side,</t>
    <t s="6">an existence of darkness and folly, etc.,</t>
    <t s="7">there must be redemption from the darkness and folly, etc.</t>
    <t s="8">And this redemption brings that holiness will be in a manner of "the advantage of light over darkness and the advantage of wisdom over folly,"</t>
    <t s="9">that is,</t>
    <t s="10">that through the redemption from darkness and folly,</t>
    <t s="11">specifically through this is made an advantage of light and wisdom,</t>
    <t s="12">and not only an advantage in quantity,</t>
    <t s="13">but also an advantage in quality.</t>
  </section>
</awtsmoosMeluketTranslation>
